paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see. Two storms in one passage, and Jesus handles both with a word. The wind and the raging waters settle and all is calm. A man chained up in the tombs, a man nobody could hold, gets set free. The disciples ask, "Who is this?" and by the end of the passage the answer is standing on a beach, because the demons themselves call Him "Jesus, Son of the Most High God" (Luke 8:28).

So why does it matter to you, baker? Because you have storms too. Some are loud, like the ones that swamp the boat. Some are quiet, like the ones that have kept a person alone for a long time. Jesus asks the disciples, "Where is your faith?" (Luke 8:25), and I think He's inviting them to trust the One who is in the boat with them, even when He looks like He's asleep.

And look at what Jesus tells the freed man to do. He doesn't get a seat in the boat. He gets a job: "Return home and describe how much God has done for you" (Luke 8:39). I know what it's like to be pulled out of the dark, and I'm telling you, you can't keep that to yourself. Whatever Jesus has done for you, baker, go tell somebody about it, because that story gets around!
